description: Tool definitions for the Claude Messages API calls n8n makes to the brain. Paste the relevant tool(s) into the n8n HTTP Request node's body under `tools`, matching brain/system_prompt.md. force tool_choice so Claude always responds structurally rather than in free text.

tools.name: submit_route_plan
tools.description: Submit the plan for which market registry routes to attempt this run, with the non-sensitive parameters each one needs. Called once per profile variant if comparing multiple vehicle/coverage scenarios in one request.

profile_label.description: Short label distinguishing this plan if multiple profile variants were requested, e.g. '2026 Chevrolet Equinox' vs '2025 Chevrolet Equinox'.

registry_id.description: Must match an id in registry/market_registry.json.

params.description: planning_safe fields only, named per schema/intake_schema.json, e.g. { "vehicle_identity.model_year": 2026, "coverage_configuration.third_party_liability_limit": 2000000 }.

reason.description: Why this route was selected for this profile.
e.g. duplicate_rate_source of another planned route, product_scope mismatch, still unresolved in the registry.

notes.description: Anything the user should know about this plan before it runs.

tools.name: submit_comparison
tools.description: Submit the normalized, deduplicated comparison across all results collected for a run.

results.description: Each item mirrors schema/quote_result_schema.json#result, enriched with dedup notes.

annual_premium.description: null if no premium was disclosed at this step — never guessed.

deductible_match.description: 'matches_benchmark', a concrete stated difference (e.g. '$1,000 collision/comprehensive deductible vs. $500 benchmark'), or 'not_disclosed'.

additional_coverage.description: Coverage included beyond the benchmark (e.g. 'roadside assistance', 'accident forgiveness'). Empty array if none observed — never omit to mean 'none'.

variance_from_benchmark.description: Every other concrete difference from the benchmark, one short statement each. Empty array only if coverage was confirmed to match exactly.

applied.description: Discounts explicitly confirmed as applied (e.g. 'winter tires'). Empty array if none confirmed.

disclosed.description: false if the route never disclosed discount info at this step — distinct from disclosing zero discounts applied.

gaps.description: Plain statements of what remains unresolved/blocked/incomplete, per docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md style — no inflation, no silent drops.

summary_text.description: Human-readable summary for the one person this system serves.

tools.name: resolve_fields
tools.description: Mid-route field resolution: the worker hit a page question it couldn't handle with its static mapping (an unrecognized field, a changed validation rule, a format mismatch, or a genuinely new question) and is asking which schema field it corresponds to and what to do. Input is structural only — question label text, field type, the site's own option list, any visible validation error text, whether the worker could tell the question is mandatory — plus profile_context: the same planning_safe facts already sent for this route during planning. Never a value, sensitive or otherwise, from either input. This tool's output must never contain a value the worker didn't already disclose either: every action must name a field for the worker to look up itself, a fixed strategy keyword, or (use_inferred_value only) one of that question's own already-disclosed options — never a literal answer invented from nothing.

question_id.description: Echoes the worker-supplied id for this question — just a correlation key, not a value.

field_mapping.description: The exact schema/intake_schema.json 'group.field' path this question corresponds to (e.g. 'risk_details.winter_tires'), or null if nothing fits. Must be a real field path — never invent one that isn't in the schema the worker will validate against.

strategy.description: 'use_mapped_field_value': the worker looks up field_mapping itself (vault or params) and types that in — you never see or supply the value. 'use_today_date'/'use_zero': the worker computes that literal itself; use for an administrative constraint no vault/schema field represents (e.g. a date within N days) — never for a question about the applicant's actual history. 'use_inferred_value': the question is genuinely answerable from profile_context alone (e.g. 'insured before?' when current_insurance.first_insured_year is present) — set inferred_value to the exact matching option from that question's own options list, never invented text. 'acknowledge_and_continue': the page is showing a non-blocking informational/confirmation banner about data already supplied (e.g. 'we noticed a gap between X and Y — if correct, continue') that isn't asking for a new value at all, just proceeding. Use only when: nothing on the page is requesting input, no checkbox/signature/consent/agreement is being agreed to, and proceeding does not submit a final application, bind a policy, or make a payment. If there's any doubt whether continuing crosses one of those lines, use pause_and_ask instead — never acknowledge_and_continue as a default when unsure. 'pause_and_ask': a mandatory question about the applicant's actual driving/claims/insurance history that profile_context doesn't answer — hand off to the human rather than guessing, favorable or not. 'skip_and_disclose': the question is optional and unanswerable — leave it blank and report why. 'unresolved': not confident enough to decide — treated the same as skip_and_disclose.

inferred_value.description: Required only when strategy is use_inferred_value. Must exactly match one entry in that question's own options list as supplied by the worker — never free text, never a value that wasn't already disclosed.

reason.description: One short, plain sentence for the run summary — why this mapping/strategy, or why it's unresolved/paused. Never repeats any value beyond a chosen inferred_value's own text; describe the situation and, for use_inferred_value, the fact it was inferred from (e.g. 'inferred Yes — current_insurance.first_insured_year is on file, so the applicant has been insured before').

tools.name: verify_carrier_quotes
tools.description: Gap-triggered vision verification for multi-carrier quote extraction: the worker's own DOM scan of a results page found more distinct price-bearing rows than it could attach a carrier name to (e.g. a stylized logo with no readable alt text or nearby label). You're given a screenshot cropped to just the results section (never the full page) plus the DOM-derived candidate list. Read the image and identify the carrier name for each row the worker couldn't name on its own. You may only ever attach a name to one of the exact dollar amounts already present in candidate_quotes or reflected in unmatched_row_count's own data — the worker discards anything else. Do not invent a premium you don't see clearly in the image, and do not guess a carrier name for a logo you can't actually read — omit that row instead. If the image is unreadable, doesn't match a quotes results page, or you're not genuinely confident in a reading, return an empty or partial quotes array rather than guessing — a missed row is far better than a wrong one.

quotes.description: Your best reading of every carrier/price/tier visible in the image, including ones the worker already matched (used only to detect disagreement worth flagging — it never overwrites the worker's own DOM-extracted value). Only entries naming a genuinely new carrier for a price the worker's own scan already found unmatched are ever added to the run's results.

underwriter.description: The insurer name as shown on its logo/label in the image, e.g. 'Sonnet', 'Gore Mutual'. Short and plain — not a sentence, not a guess dressed up as a name.

annual_premium.description: The annual premium in dollars for this row, read from the image (convert a monthly figure ×12 if that's the only one shown) — must match a real figure visible in the image, never estimated.

package_tier.description: Which of the two tiers this row belongs to, based on the image's own labelling.

tools.name: flag_new_field
tools.description: Raise an anomaly: input contained something that looks sensitive or unrecognized rather than a clean planning_safe field. Never process the suspected value — only describe what was observed. Call this ONLY when something genuinely looks wrong. Never call it to confirm that nothing is wrong, and never call it just because the tool is available — if every field looks like a clean planning_safe value, simply don't call this tool at all this turn. This tool triggers the pipeline to halt the entire run, so an unnecessary call has a real cost, not just a harmless note.

observed_at.description: Where in the input this was seen, e.g. 'route plan request, field vehicle_identity.owner_name'. Never a placeholder like 'N/A' or 'none' — if there's no real location because nothing is actually wrong, don't call this tool at all.

description.description: What made this look sensitive or unrecognized — never repeat the actual value.
